acp-105.summary: An experimental partial-agonist SARM that users take for lean mass with milder androgenic effects; studied in rats and mice, sold online as a research chemical.

quick.overview:
ACP-105 is a selective androgen receptor modulator (SARM) from the late 2000s. People take it hoping for more lean muscle and a leaner, harder look, with gentler androgenic effects than testosterone.

It works as a partial agonist at the androgen receptor, switching on muscle-building signalling more weakly than testosterone does. In castrated rats and mice it improved anabolic markers, and later animal work looked at cognitive decline and radiation-related deficits. No human trials have been published.
quick.how: Users describe it as an oral research chemical bought online and taken alongside resistance training, often during a lean-gain or recomposition phase. Reports of when changes show up vary, and no human protocol exists.
quick.risks: Human safety is unknown. SARMs as a class are banned in sport and have been linked in reports to liver injury and suppressed natural hormones. ACP-105 is unapproved and sold only as a research chemical.

angle.text: ACP-105 is a partial-agonist SARM that users take to add lean mass with milder androgenic effects. It partially activates the androgen receptor, which in castrated rats and mice improved anabolic markers and could translate to more muscle. Research so far is animal-only.

ac-262536.summary: An Acadia-developed SARM that users take for lean muscle gain with smaller prostate effects; studied in rats, sold online as a research chemical.

quick.overview:
AC-262,536 is a SARM from Acadia Pharmaceuticals that users take in pursuit of lean muscle and a more muscular physique, with less androgenic impact on tissues like the prostate than testosterone.

It is a partial agonist at the androgen receptor. In a two-week study in castrated rats it improved anabolic parameters, with a reported maximal effect on muscle weight of about 66% of testosterone's versus about 27% for prostate weight. No human trial has been published.
quick.how: Users describe it as an oral research chemical taken with resistance training during lean-gain phases. Reported timelines come from user accounts, not trials.
quick.risks: Human safety is unknown. It is unapproved and banned in sport, and SARMs as a class are linked in reports to liver injury and hormone suppression. It has been sold as a designer drug online.

angle.text: AC-262,536 is a SARM that users take to build lean muscle. It partially activates the androgen receptor, which in castrated rats improved anabolic parameters in a two-week study, with a stronger effect on muscle than on the prostate. Human data have not been published.

bms-564929.summary: A very potent Bristol-Myers Squibb SARM that drives muscle growth in rats with little prostate stimulation; its early human trial was discontinued.

quick.overview:
BMS-564929 is a highly potent oral SARM that muscle-building users mention for strong muscle stimulation with little prostate stimulation. Bristol-Myers Squibb developed it for age-related decline.

It binds the androgen receptor with subnanomolar affinity and is selective over other steroid receptors. A 2007 study in castrated rats reported strong skeletal muscle stimulation with comparatively little prostate effect. It entered Phase I, which was discontinued, and no results are public.
quick.how: Users who mention it describe taking it orally as a research chemical alongside resistance training for lean-mass phases. There is no published human protocol.
quick.risks: Strong suppression of luteinizing hormone has been reported, so natural testosterone signalling can drop. Human safety is unpublished. It is unapproved and banned in sport.

angle.text: BMS-564929 is a highly potent SARM that muscle-building users mention for strong muscle stimulation with little prostate effect. It binds the androgen receptor very tightly, which drove muscle growth in castrated rats. It was developed for age-related decline, and its Phase I trial was discontinued.

glpg0492.summary: An experimental non-steroidal SARM studied for muscle wasting that users take to build muscle with weaker prostate effects; tested in mice and phase 1 volunteer trials.

quick.overview:
GLPG0492 (DT-200) is a non-steroidal SARM designed to build muscle through the androgen receptor with weaker effects on the prostate and reproductive tissue than testosterone. It has been investigated for sarcopenia, cachexia and muscular dystrophy.

It binds the androgen receptor as a partial agonist. In rodents it increased muscle measures and strength, with reduced effects on reproductive organs compared with testosterone-type comparators. Research consists of rodent studies and three phase 1 trials in healthy volunteers; no published trial has measured muscle or appearance in people.
quick.how: Users who follow it describe it as an oral research compound taken with resistance training for lean mass. No human protocol has been published.
quick.risks: Published sources do not summarize human safety data. It is not approved for any use, and SARMs are subject to anti-doping testing.

angle.text: GLPG0492 is a non-steroidal SARM that users take hoping to build muscle with weaker effects on the prostate. It activates the androgen receptor in muscle, and in rodents it raised muscle measures and strength. It was studied in mouse muscle-wasting models and phase 1 volunteer trials.

tfm-4as-1.summary: A laboratory steroidal SARM that favored muscle and bone over reproductive tissue in rats; not yet studied in people.

quick.overview:
TFM-4AS-1 is a steroidal SARM that muscle-building readers cite for adding muscle and bone while having smaller effects on reproductive organs and oil-producing skin glands in rats.

It partially activates the androgen receptor and blocks the receptor's internal N/C-terminal interaction, so only some androgen-responsive genes switch on. A 2009 Journal of Biological Chemistry study found ovariectomized rats gained bone and muscle mass without prostate growth. No human study exists.
quick.how: It is a laboratory compound with no established routine. Any physique use is discussed from the rat work.
quick.risks: Human safety is unknown. It is not approved for any use.

angle.text: TFM-4AS-1 is a steroidal SARM that muscle-building readers cite for adding muscle and bone while sparing reproductive tissue in rats. It partially activates the androgen receptor, switching on only some androgen-responsive genes. Research is limited to laboratory work.

mk-0773.summary: A steroidal SARM that added lean mass in frail older women in a phase 2 trial, though strength and function did not improve beyond placebo.

quick.overview:
MK-0773 is a steroidal SARM tested for sarcopenia, the loss of muscle with age. It is the kind of lean-mass gain physique-focused users look for, and it is followed as a human-data example.

It was selected in 2010 from a screen of more than 1,000 synthetic androgen receptor ligands for separable anabolic and reproductive-tissue effects. In a phase 2A trial of 170 frail older women with sarcopenia, lean body mass rose compared with placebo, but strength and physical function did not improve beyond placebo.
quick.how: It was given in a clinical trial setting. It is not sold as a product, and there is no routine for physique use.
quick.risks: Safety data from the efficacy trial are not detailed in published sources reviewed. It is not approved for any use and is covered by anti-doping testing.

angle.text: MK-0773 is a steroidal SARM that activates the androgen receptor and raised lean mass in frail older women in a phase 2 sarcopenia trial. Strength and function did not improve beyond placebo in that trial, and the participants were not people seeking a physique.

gsk2881078.summary: A pharma-developed SARM that raised lean mass in older adults and leg strength in men with COPD, with lower HDL and transient liver-enzyme rises reported.

quick.overview:
GSK2881078 is a non-steroidal SARM from GlaxoSmithKline, built for muscle weakness in chronic and acute illness. Muscle-focused readers cite it as one of the better human data sets for a SARM.

It acts on the androgen receptor to promote muscle growth and has a very long half-life, reported at over 100 hours. In healthy older adults it produced dose-dependent lean mass gains over placebo, and in a 13-week trial in men with COPD it increased leg strength beyond exercise alone, though patient-reported outcomes did not change. Trials were in older or ill people, not people seeking a cosmetic physique.
quick.how: It was given in clinical trials, often alongside an exercise program in the COPD study. It is not a marketed product.
quick.risks: Trials reported lowered HDL cholesterol and sex hormone-binding globulin, transient ALT liver-enzyme elevations and, in one case, a drug rash. It is not approved, and SARM safety reviews cite liver injury and tendon rupture cases with recreational SARM use.

angle.text: GSK2881078 is a SARM that activates the androgen receptor and raised lean mass in older adults and leg strength in men with COPD, so muscle-focused readers cite it as a human data set. Trials were in ill or older people rather than people seeking a cosmetic physique.

opk-88004.summary: An investigational SARM that raised lean mass and reduced fat in prostate cancer survivors, though symptoms and performance did not improve.

quick.overview:
OPK-88004 is an oral non-steroidal SARM that increased lean mass and lowered fat mass in testosterone-deficient prostate cancer survivors, the body-composition change SARM followers look for: leaner and more muscular.

It is intended to act on muscle with less effect on the prostate. In a randomized trial of 114 men who had prostatectomy for low-grade prostate cancer, lean body mass rose and fat mass fell, but sexual symptoms and physical performance did not improve. A phase 2 BPH trial was terminated. It has not been studied for appearance.
quick.how: It was given orally in clinical trials. It is not marketed, and no routine for physique use exists.
quick.risks: The survivor trial reported no PSA recurrence or erythrocytosis. Oral SARMs have been reported to suppress HDL cholesterol. It is not approved for any use.

angle.text: OPK-88004 is a SARM that activates the androgen receptor and raised lean mass while reducing fat in prostate cancer survivors, giving a leaner, more muscular body composition. Symptoms and physical performance did not improve in that trial, and appearance was not studied.

mk-3984.summary: An obscure SARM candidate aimed at muscle and bone, known mainly from a doping-control metabolite study; no human data.

quick.overview:
MK-3984 is a little-documented SARM candidate targeting muscle and bone, which muscle-building communities occasionally list as a lean-mass candidate.

As a SARM it is designed to act on androgen receptors in muscle and bone. The only dedicated study found is a 2026 doping-control study mapping its metabolism in zebrafish. No clinical trials or human data exist.
quick.how: There is no established routine; it appears mainly in discussions of lesser-known SARMs.
quick.risks: Human safety is unknown, and it is not approved for any use.

angle.text: MK-3984 is an obscure SARM that muscle-building communities occasionally list as a lean-mass candidate. It is designed to act on androgen receptors in muscle and bone. Published work is limited to a doping-control metabolite study in zebrafish, with no human data.

arcarine.summary: Orion's discontinued SARM candidate aimed at selective muscle and bone activation; reached Phase I and left almost no public data.

quick.overview:
Arcarine (ORM-11984) is a SARM from Orion Corporation that muscle-building readers know as a discontinued candidate for selective androgen receptor activation in tissues like muscle and bone.

Orion developed it for benign prostatic hyperplasia, hypogonadism and osteoporosis. It reached Phase I trials before development was discontinued, and its structure was never disclosed. A rat study of local delivery reported it did not act as an anabolic agent in that model. No data on muscle or appearance have been published.
quick.how: It is not a marketed product, and no routine for physique use exists.
quick.risks: No safety data are published. SARMs as a class are unapproved, banned by WADA, and linked in case reports to liver injury with recreational use.

angle.text: Arcarine (ORM-11984) is a SARM from Orion that muscle-building readers know as a discontinued candidate for selective androgen receptor activation in muscle and bone. It reached Phase I and left almost no public data on muscle or appearance.

gsk-971086.summary: A discontinued GSK indole-class SARM studied for sarcopenia and androgen deficiency; never got past Phase I.

quick.overview:
GSK-971086 is an indole-class SARM from GlaxoSmithKline, investigated for sarcopenia and androgen deficiency and followed by muscle-building readers as a lean-mass candidate.

SARMs aim to switch on androgen receptors selectively, favoring muscle and bone over reproductive tissue. A Phase I trial registered in 2007 tested safety, tolerability and blood levels in healthy men after a single dose and after seven days of dosing. Development was then discontinued, and no muscle or appearance results are published.
quick.how: It is not a marketed drug, and no routine for physique use exists.
quick.risks: No Phase I results are public in the sources reviewed. The SARM class is unapproved, banned in sport by WADA, and linked in case reports to liver injury with recreational use.

angle.text: GSK-971086 is an indole-class SARM investigated for sarcopenia and androgen deficiency, followed by muscle-building readers as a lean-mass candidate. It activates the androgen receptor selectively, but development stopped after a Phase I safety trial and no efficacy data exist.

gsk-2849466.summary: A GSK SARM candidate for cachexia and heart failure that stopped after one small Phase I trial.

quick.overview:
GSK-2849466 is a SARM from GlaxoSmithKline studied for cachexia and heart failure, which muscle-focused readers note as a lean-mass candidate.

It belongs to the N-arylhydroxyalkyl class and is meant to activate androgen receptors preferentially in muscle and bone rather than reproductive tissue. A Phase I trial begun in 2012 tested safety, tolerability and pharmacokinetics in 17 healthy men, after which development was discontinued. No appearance-related data exist.
quick.how: It is not marketed, and no routine for physique use exists.
quick.risks: No trial results are published in the sources reviewed. The SARM class is unapproved, banned by WADA, and associated in case reports with liver injury from recreational use.

angle.text: GSK-2849466 is a SARM investigated for cachexia and heart failure, noted by muscle-focused readers as a lean-mass candidate. It is meant to activate androgen receptors in muscle and bone. Development stopped after one small Phase I trial in 17 healthy men.

gtx-027.summary: A SARM candidate explored for breast cancer and stress urinary incontinence; mostly preclinical, with no data on muscle or looks.

quick.overview:
GTx-027 is an arylpropionamide-class SARM associated with GTx, Inc., investigated for breast cancer and stress urinary incontinence and occasionally listed by muscle-building readers among SARMs.

SARMs are designed to activate androgen receptors selectively. A 2017 mouse study examined whether tissue-selective SARMs increase pelvic floor muscle mass in ovariectomized mice. Its status is listed as Phase I, discontinued, or preclinical, and no human trial on muscle or appearance exists.
quick.how: It is not marketed, and no routine for physique use exists.
quick.risks: No human safety data are available in the sources reviewed. The SARM class is unapproved, banned by WADA, and linked in case reports to liver injury with recreational use.

angle.text: GTx-027 is a SARM explored for breast cancer and stress urinary incontinence, occasionally listed by muscle-building readers. It activates androgen receptors, and mouse work on SARMs reported more pelvic floor muscle mass. It is largely preclinical, with no data on physique.

ly305.summary: A skin-applied SARM built for low testosterone and explored for muscle wasting; no appearance data.

quick.overview:
LY305 is an N-arylhydroxyalkyl SARM designed to be applied through the skin for men with low testosterone, and also explored for muscle wasting and osteoporosis. That makes it of interest to people chasing a muscle and hormone-related physique.

It activates the androgen receptor. A 2018 paper described it as bioavailable by the transdermal route while being cleared extensively by the liver, a design meant to limit liver exposure to the parent compound. Wikipedia reports promising Phase I results. No appearance trials have been published.
quick.how: It is an investigational product, not sold for use. No routine for physique use exists.
quick.risks: Little human safety data is public. SARMs are unapproved and banned by WADA, and a 2025 study characterized its metabolism to support doping control.

angle.text: LY305 is a SARM built as a skin-applied treatment for low testosterone, which interests people seeking a muscle and hormone-related physique. It activates the androgen receptor and was also explored for muscle wasting. Appearance has not been studied.

pf-06260414.summary: Pfizer's oral SARM for cachexia; safety-tested in healthy men, then shelved.

quick.overview:
PF-06260414 is an oral SARM from Pfizer, studied for cachexia, which muscle-building readers follow as a lean-mass candidate.

It belongs to the isoquinoline class and is designed to activate androgen receptors preferentially in muscle and bone. A 2016 paper reported tolerability, pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic results from single and multiple ascending oral doses in healthy men. Development was discontinued after Phase I, and efficacy was never tested in trials.
quick.how: It was given orally in a clinical setting. It is not marketed, and no routine for physique use exists.
quick.risks: Only Phase I tolerability data exist. The SARM class is unapproved and banned by WADA, with case reports of liver injury from recreational use.

angle.text: PF-06260414 is Pfizer's oral SARM, studied for cachexia and designed to activate androgen receptors in muscle and bone. Muscle-building readers follow it as a lean-mass candidate. It was safety-tested in healthy men and shelved after Phase I, with no appearance data.

jnj-26146900.summary: A Johnson & Johnson SARM studied in rats as a prostate cancer drug, with anabolic effects on muscle and bone in animals; never given to humans.

quick.overview:
JNJ-26146900 is a SARM that Johnson & Johnson studied as a possible prostate cancer drug. Muscle-building readers note it for its androgen receptor selectivity and tissue-specific effects.

It binds the androgen receptor and acts differently by tissue: antagonist-like in the prostate, with anabolic effects reported in muscle and bone in animals. In a 2007 rat study it reduced prostate weight and tumor size and prevented some bone loss after castration. It was never marketed, and no human data exist.
quick.how: It is a research compound with no established routine. Physique discussions rest on the rat work.
quick.risks: Human safety has not been studied. It is not approved for any use.

angle.text: JNJ-26146900 is a SARM investigated for prostate cancer and noted by muscle-building readers for its androgen receptor selectivity. In rats it acted antagonist-like in the prostate while showing anabolic effects on muscle and bone. It was studied only in animals.

ru-59063.summary: A 1990s research androgen-receptor ligand, sometimes classed as a SARM, that became a template for later antiandrogens; no human use.

quick.overview:
RU-59063 is an early nonsteroidal compound that binds the androgen receptor very tightly. It is sometimes classed as a SARM, and muscle circles occasionally link it to lean mass, though that link is theoretical.

It was first described in 1994, derived from the antiandrogen nilutamide, and bound the rat androgen receptor with up to about three times the affinity of testosterone, with mixed antagonist and weak agonist behaviour. Its main significance is as a starting point for later drugs such as enzalutamide and apalutamide, and for radioligand research. No muscle or appearance studies in people exist.
quick.how: It is a laboratory compound that was never marketed, so there is no routine for use.
quick.risks: Human safety is unstudied, and it has no approved use.

angle.text: RU-59063 is a 1990s research androgen-receptor ligand, sometimes classed as a SARM, which muscle circles occasionally link to lean mass. It binds the androgen receptor tightly and became a template for later antiandrogens. It has no human use, and its appearance link is theoretical.

bolandiol.summary: A nandrolone-related steroid with mixed androgen, estrogen and progestin activity; raised lean mass in rats, never marketed as a base.

quick.overview:
Bolandiol is a nandrolone-like anabolic steroid that physique-focused readers discuss as an anabolic. Its dipropionate ester has been sold in the past, but the base compound never was.

It binds the androgen receptor weakly but also has estrogenic and progestational activity. In castrated adult male rats it raised lean mass and bone mineral density without strongly stimulating sex accessory glands. Wikipedia reports that several clinical studies found no change in strength, body composition or exercise performance.
quick.how: Past sales were of the dipropionate ester; no current routine is established.
quick.risks: It suppresses gonadotropins and natural testosterone in animals. It is on the WADA prohibited list.

angle.text: Bolandiol is a nandrolone-related steroid with mixed androgen, estrogen and progestin activity, discussed by physique-focused readers as an anabolic. In castrated rats it raised lean mass and bone density, while Wikipedia reports clinical studies found no change in strength or body composition.

dienolone.summary: A never-marketed nandrolone-like steroid, mainly of interest as a chemical intermediate.

quick.overview:
Dienolone is a 19-nortestosterone steroid that physique readers mention for its anabolic class. It was developed under the code RU-3118 and never sold as a drug.

Based on rat and rabbit tissue assays, it binds androgen and progesterone receptors slightly less strongly than nandrolone. Its main role in the literature is as a chemical intermediate, including in routes to trenbolone and other steroids. No human data exist.
quick.how: It was never marketed, so there is no routine for use.
quick.risks: Human safety is unstudied.

angle.text: Dienolone is a nandrolone-like steroid that physique readers mention for its anabolic class. It binds androgen receptors slightly less strongly than nandrolone in animal tissue assays. It was never marketed and is known mainly as a chemical intermediate; no human data exist.

norclostebol.summary: A 1950s chlorinated nandrolone derivative described as strongly anabolic and weakly androgenic; no listed medical use and no human studies.

quick.overview:
Norclostebol is a chlorinated derivative of nandrolone, described in 1957 and sold under names such as Lentabol. Physique readers mention it for its anabolic class, reported as strongly anabolic and weakly androgenic.

Wikipedia lists no medical uses. Its acetate ester was reported on the European black market in the late 1990s, and the main published work concerns detecting its illegal use in cattle, including a 2006 study of urinary metabolites. No human studies of muscle or appearance exist.
quick.how: It has no listed medical use and no established routine.
quick.risks: No human safety studies were found.

angle.text: Norclostebol is a chlorinated nandrolone derivative described in 1957 and reported as strongly anabolic and weakly androgenic, which is why physique readers mention it. It has no listed medical use, and published work mostly concerns detecting it in cattle.
